title: Corn, frozen, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Corn is a globally cultivated grain. This product consists of frozen, cooked corn kernels with added vegetable fat to improve flavor and texture. It is ready to eat after heating and is often used as a side dish or ingredient in various recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the most widely consumed crops worldwide and forms a staple in many countries.
Frozen cooked kernels retain most of their vitamins and minerals thanks to rapid processing after harvest.
Adding fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and E.
Corn is used to produce starch, syrups, and bio‑fuel.
There are over 300 corn varieties differing in color, sweetness, and texture.

items.title: Rich source of carbohydrates
items.content: Corn provides a quick source of energy due to its high complex carbohydrate content.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamin, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added fat improves the bioavailability of vitamins A and E, beneficial for vision and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Corn provides magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting muscle and heart function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Because the product contains added fat, people monitoring calorie intake should account for it in their diet.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn has a relatively high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready after heating in the microwave or on the stove. It can be added to salads, soups, stews, used as a side dish for meat or fish, or incorporated into tacos and burritos.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen corn at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze. Discard if it develops off‑odors or discoloration.
